answer.rationale: Write-path p99 climbing since shortly after a release 2 hours ago strongly suggests the new build, matching memory_b1's precedent where rollback cleared a latency/error regression without customer impact. Failover (b2) addresses regional issues, not a suspect build; circuit breakers (b4) target dependency outages, not the write path; read-replica routing (b5) relieves read load only; added capacity (b3) risks masking a code regression at peak settlement. However, settlement peak is a confounder, so I verify b1 (rollback safety) and b3 (capacity-vs-regression precedent) before committing. Rollback preserves in-flight customer writes (schema-compatible prior build per b1 precedent), but I flag downstream risk: if the release included write-schema changes, rollback could jeopardize recent writes — this must be checked before execution. Rollback executed as a guarded, monitored step with immediate p99 and error-rate verification rather than assumed success.
